cover letter
Advanced degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
Demonstrated experience in software system design, implementation, testing, and debugging.
Demonstrated experience with Python programming language.
Advanced interpersonal skills, including the ability to work in a collaborative manner with colleagues of diverse backgrounds and levels of experience.
Experience with telescopes and/or astronomical instrumentation, or functionally similar systems.
Experience supporting operating software with a staff and user community in a research environment like an observatory or similar facility.
Experience working on a distributed team, possibly in different time zones, using distributed work platforms such as wikis, Zoom, Slack, SharePoint, Google and Atlassian products, etc.
Experience evaluating the performance of a software system, summarizing that information, presenting to users and other consumers of that information, and monitoring performance over time.
Experience with networking, operating systems and other computing infrastructure used in a research software environment.
Experience with software development tools in standard use.
Experience with the Linux operating system.

The University of California Observatories (UCO) Observatory and Instrumentation Software Engineer supports and develops software for astronomical instruments and observatories. UCO Software Engineers enthusiastically face the challenges at research observatories through hands-on work on all phases of a project: requirements development, concept design, code implementation, system integration, testing, troubleshooting, performance monitoring and upgrades. The software engineering group works on a broad range of complex technical challenges supporting one-of-a kind-systems. Areas of focus include adaptive optics, precision motion control of electronic, optical and mechanical systems, detector evaluation and optimization, acquisition and analysis of test and scientific data, automated telescope scheduling and operations, data archiving, observatory environment control and monitoring, and development of user interfaces.
Strong creativity and problem solving abilities.
Familiarity with C and C++.
Selected candidate will be required to pass a pre-employment criminal history background check.
Selected candidate must pass the employment misconduct disclosure process.

The selected candidate will be required to work primarily on campus, with periods of remote work possible based on operational needs. If a hybrid work schedule is confirmed, the selected candidate must be able to work successfully from a home/remote office and be able to fulfill the requirements of the UCSC telecommuting agreement.
Selected candidate will be required to complete training within established time frames as directed including UC compliance training.

The University of California has implemented a Vaccination Policy covering all employees. Employees, including new hires, are required to comply with any applicable policies relating to the University of California vaccine program.

Per the Child Abuse and Neglect Reporting Act (CANRA), this position has been identified as a Mandated Reporter. The selected candidate will be required to report known or suspected child abuse or neglect as defined by CANRA and will be required to sign a Statement Acknowledging Requirement to Report Child Abuse prior to commencing employment. CANRA Penal Codes, and related definitions, requirements, and responsibilities may be obtained here.
Ability to collaborate effectively with faculty, staff, and students in a research environment to address open-ended problems with few or changing requirements to forward the ultimate research goal.
Ability to work on site at telescope locations (including Maunakea, Hawai'i) in cold and difficult conditions.
Demonstrated ability to generate clear and concise technical documents and presentations, including internal reports, external design review documentation, and journal publications.
Ability to work long periods of time at a computer with or without accommodation.
Advanced communication skills to convey complex information in a clear and concise manner.
Ability to travel nationally.
